tiers.skill_structural: Graded ONLY for with_skill runs. Verifies template formatting, versioning, issue IDs. NOT used in cross-config comparison.
tiers.content_quality: Graded for BOTH configs. Ground-truth findings, severity accuracy, no false positives, project-rules awareness. This is the real comparison.
tiers.consistency: Graded across multiple runs of same config. Same critical issues found, same severity classifications. Requires 3+ runs.

ground_truth_issues: Unbounded recursive retry in ShopifyProductGatewayAdapter.fetchProductPage() — real bug, all runs should find it
No error handling in ProductImportWorker.execute() — jobs stuck in IN_PROGRESS forever
GraphQL page size of 5 (Shopify supports 250) — massive performance gap
N+1 variant upserts — individual SQL per variant in a loop
@Entity on ImportJob in domain layer — pre-existing tech debt (Product.java does the same)
ProductImportConsumer injects concrete class, not port interface — architecture violation
Missing input validation on Work Queue endpoint — security gap

evals.name: full-review-product-import
evals.prompt: Review my changes on this branch. I've been building a product import pipeline — it fetches products from Shopify's GraphQL API, maps them to our domain, and persists them. The changes span domain models, ports, application services, infrastructure adapters, and tests.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive review covering all 5 scopes with ground-truth issues identified, severity proportional to impact, pre-existing patterns classified as tech debt, and project-specific rules cited.

evals.name: scoped-review-security-architecture
evals.prompt: Review my changes but focus only on security and architecture. I want to make sure the hexagonal architecture is respected and there are no security issues before I submit the PR.
evals.expected_output: A review covering ONLY architecture and security with port/adapter violations identified, input validation gaps caught, and @Entity-on-domain handled as tech debt.

evals.name: targeted-review-performance
evals.prompt: Can you review ProductImportWorker.java for performance issues? It's the core loop that fetches pages of products from Shopify and persists them. I'm worried about N+1 queries and rate limiting.
evals.expected_output: A focused performance review of the import worker finding N+1 patterns, page size issues, and accurately describing rate limiting — with no scope leakage into other review areas.
